prerequisites: Having taken Physics and Mathematics courses during high school.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to work in a team

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation professionally and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study

Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems
Ability to apply knowledge in practice
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language
Ability to fluently use computing at a user level
Be able to comprehensibly explain phenomena and processes related to the basic aspects of Physics using appropriate magnitudes and units.
Ability to solve Physics problems that reinforce theoretical knowledge and serve as an introduction to subsequent applications of interest for engineering.
Analyze physical phenomena and take experimental data for their study.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 1: INTRODUCTION TO PHYSICS. Vector calculus.
TOPIC 2: PARTICLE KINEMATICS. General concepts. Study of movements.
TOPIC 3: PARTICLE DYNAMICS. Newton's principles. Work and energy.
TOPIC 4: DYNAMICS OF PARTICLE SYSTEMS. General study. Collisions.
TOPIC 5: RIGID BODY DYNAMICS. Rigid body rotation.
TOPIC 6: SIMPLE HARMONIC MOTION Study of SHM in springs. Study of SHM in pendulums.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on laboratory practices (15%) and a final written exam (85%). The final exam consists of a multiple-choice part and an exercise-solving part. Laboratory practices are evaluated through follow-up and critical assessment of submitted reports and proposed questions.
